facts.subject: opening
facts.fact: Alistair was summoned with the four heroes; Court Mage Serika Amamiya's appraisal lens went dark on him and she called it a summoning error, a fragment pulled through by accident.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: gold pouch
facts.fact: Court Mage Serika Amamiya pressed a pouch of twenty-five gold into Alistair's palm and suggested the service sector; the Guild registers anyone.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: palace wards
facts.fact: The palace wards and crystals pass over Alistair; his Living Relic Blade thrums at its side, its indignation felt only by him.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: Toma protest
facts.fact: Toma objected openly in the throne room that Alistair came through with them and is part of the count; Yui said the decision was made before the light faded.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: Suzuha asked his name
facts.fact: Princess Suzuha Sumeragi stopped the guards and asked Alistair's name, calling him 'collateral'.
facts.evidence: Voyage opening narration

facts.subject: Toma's snack
facts.fact: Toma waited at the side door and gave Alistair a warm cloth-wrapped snack of bread and salted meat (eat before noon), saying the Guild registers anyone: 'That's not exile, that's a door. Doors work both ways.'
facts.evidence: Toma presses a cloth-wrapped snack into Alistair's hand

facts.subject: Suzuha's order
facts.fact: Suzuha, no warmth, ordered the guards to see that Alistair passes unharmed, then added 'If convenient' a half-second late; Court Mage Serika Amamiya declared the matter closed and ordered the misfire logged.
facts.evidence: Suzuha: 'Guards, see that he passes unharmed.' ... 'If convenient.'

facts.subject: Daigo's jab
facts.fact: Daigo jeered 'Hey, zero! At least tip the pouch on your way out!' and then went quiet; nobody laughed. Yui watched the pouch's weight and filed the number away.
facts.evidence: Daigo: brittle bravado; Yui fixes on the pouch's weight

facts.subject: Rin at the window
facts.fact: Rin watched Alistair leave from a high window, jaw set, thumb running along her sword guard.
facts.evidence: High above, through a window slit, Rin watches

facts.subject: Toma's offer
facts.fact: Toma offered Alistair one favor, one contact or one honest answer, whenever he wants it, no clock on it; Alistair said he will take him up on it one day.
facts.evidence: Toma: 'one favor, one contact, or one honest answer whenever you want it' / Alistair: 'I'll take you up on it one day'

facts.subject: Toma's warning
facts.fact: Toma warned Alistair that a grand campaign of frontier dungeons and demon-border work is coming and the Crown will spend the heroes like coin; watch who spends you. Toma said aloud at the Guild that cutting Alistair from the roster was wrong.
facts.evidence: Toma at the counter: 'watch who spends you'

facts.subject: Mizuho's first words
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku, head of the main counter at the Aureliath branch of the Adventurer's Guild, read Alistair's gear in one glance, said his sword is better cared for than he looks rested, folded a rejected application into a paper crane, and told him the form can wait until she knows what she is stamping.
facts.evidence: Mizuho's greeting at the counter

facts.subject: Toma's strap
facts.fact: Toma tightened a loose strap on Alistair's pauldron unasked ('Would've rattled loose by noon'), told him 'Eat well. Register loud', and left the Guild Hall under a plain grey cloak to return to the palace before he is missed.
facts.evidence: Toma tugs the pauldron strap, then heads out through the doors

facts.subject: Mizuho knows Toma is a hero
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku recognised Toma as a Hero of the Realm, watched the door three seconds too long, and asked Alistair for his name and what he needs (registration, contract board access, or just admiring the paperwork); she told him to choose his first job like it matters.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'first time a Hero of the Realm has done my queue-jumping for me' ... 'Choose your first job like it matters.'

facts.subject: Guild registration rules
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku explained that registration puts Alistair in the Guild's book (rank card, bank access, quest board rights); everyone starts at F-Rank; the Guild keeps no file on what the Crown discards ('what they log at the palace stays at the palace').
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'Registration puts you in our book. Rank card, bank access, quest board rights. F-Rank to start'

facts.subject: Mizuho's lesson
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku told Alistair 'Rank is just a number. Whether you come back is a habit', 'I stamp people alive, not clever', to pick something small for his first job and not die before she has learned his name; she set a folded paper crane on the counter between them like a marker on a map.
facts.evidence: Mizuho's counter lesson and the crane

facts.subject: Alistair registered
facts.fact: Alistair Zebias is a registered F-Rank adventurer with a plain iron card, no party; Mizuho corrected his form ('officially employed as loneliness') and stamped it.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'Alistair Zebias, F-Rank, no party, one very good sword.'

facts.subject: Kazuki met
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara, a first-day F-Rank like Alistair, introduced himself at the notice board, called the rat culls bad pay but safe, and said of the unstamped slip: no stamp means no escrow, and the Guild never heard of you; his 'auntie-clerk' (Mizuho) would fold a hundred cranes.
facts.evidence: Kazuki's chat at the posting wall

facts.subject: unstamped slip
facts.fact: A plain-sealed slip with no counter stamp hangs on the Guild notice board between a lost-cat job and a herb-gathering contract; nobody takes it. A runner tapped it twice before leaving.
facts.evidence: The runner taps one slip twice before leaving - a plain-sealed paper with no counter stamp

facts.subject: the dusk slip
facts.fact: Alistair took the unstamped slip off the Guild notice board on Day 1. Terms: a quiet courier errand at dusk, one delivery, no questions; gold pay above any F-Rank posting's monthly pay; 'ask for the courier in grey'; no Guild seal.
facts.evidence: He unfolds the parchment: a quiet courier errand at dusk, one delivery, no questions ... ask for the courier in grey

facts.subject: Mizuho on the slip
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku saw Alistair take the slip, called him to the counter very politely, held out her palm for it, and called it 'bait with a price tag'; she asked who posts jobs behind her counter with no stamp, no escrow and no name.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'That's not a contract. That's bait with a price tag.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's reaction
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara laughed nervously, said people take such slips all the time, 'probably', and his eyes flicked to the gold figure on the slip.
facts.evidence: Kazuki: 'It's fine! People take those all the time. Probably.'

facts.subject: Mizuho's condition
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku will not stamp the unstamped slip and will not say why, but does not forbid it ('F-Rank means you're free to make your own mistakes'). Condition: if Alistair takes it, he comes back to her counter afterward and tells her whom he meets, 'not for the Guild, for me'.
facts.evidence: Mizuho: 'I won't stamp it. I won't tell you why ... One condition.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's bun
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara offered Alistair half his meat bun ('You look like you skipped breakfast chasing gold') and remarked that nobody is hungry enough yet to take that slip; give it a week and the food starts sounding better.
facts.evidence: Kazuki tears his meat bun in half and holds one piece out

facts.subject: the runner
facts.fact: A runner who tapped the slip earlier lingered by the great doors watching the counter exchange, then slipped out into the square.
facts.evidence: By the great doors, the runner lingers just inside the threshold

facts.subject: courier in grey
facts.fact: At dusk on Day 1 a courier in grey (white half-mask, small brass lantern, masculine, soft and level) met Alistair at the lamplit edge of the Guild Quarter square: 'You would be the one who took the slip... Most stare at it for a week and choose the rats.' He offered tea and asked whether Alistair carries the slip ('Some prefer to memorize and burn. Only honesty is required.').
facts.evidence: COURIER IN GREY dialogue

facts.subject: Mizuho's crane
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku said 'Counter. Tomorrow. Tell me.' and left a folded paper crane facing the door on the counter; Alistair owes her a report on whom he meets (quest 'The Quiet Posting').
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'Counter. Tomorrow. Tell me.'

facts.subject: courier's terms
facts.fact: The courier in grey would not name the sender ('prefers quiet'), set a small case sealed with grey wax and a purse of good-faith gold on the cobblestones, and said the purse is Alistair's whether he hands over the slip or only its contents; the case travels back with his answer. 'Honesty is the only currency I require. Lie to me, and the work ends tonight. Tell me true, and there may be more work after.'
facts.evidence: COURIER IN GREY dialogue on trust and the case and purse

facts.subject: courier's lantern
facts.fact: The flame in the courier's brass lantern stays perfectly still even when the evening breeze tugs at every other lamp.
facts.evidence: the flame inside the courier's brass lantern stands perfectly still

facts.subject: slip handed over
facts.fact: Alistair handed the courier in grey the slip and took the purse of fresh-minted gold; the courier said 'Received and paid. The sender will be satisfied' and asked one question: does anyone expect Alistair home tonight? No ambush.
facts.evidence: Courier: 'Received and paid.' ... 'Does anyone expect you home tonight?'

facts.subject: courier's parting
facts.fact: The courier in grey said errands run long and he likes to know whom to send word to; he recorded Alistair's silence as honest, took the sealed case and left down a side street. More work waits wherever grey stands at a crowd's edge; no sender and no place named. Alistair refused the tea and thanked him.
facts.evidence: Courier: 'Silence is honest too. I'll record it as such.' / Alistair rejects tea

facts.subject: inn terms
facts.fact: A plain Guild Quarter inn: bed three silver, supper one silver more, breakfast included before the sixth bell, room left of the stairs; 'No questions asked here, no questions answered either.'
facts.evidence: INNKEEPER: 'Bed's three silver, supper's one more...'

facts.subject: Kazuki's seat
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara, alone at a corner table, saved Alistair a seat by the wall ('no pressure') and greeted him as 'senior'; his eyes kept flicking toward the door.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'Senior! You made it back in one piece.'

facts.subject: public gossip
facts.fact: Gossip in the inn: the palace side door opened for somebody this morning; the summoning produced four heroes and a 'fifth one' who read a flat zero; people glance at Alistair's sword, which doesn't look guild-issued.
facts.evidence: MERCHANT: 'the fifth one they pulled through came up a flat zero'

facts.subject: Kazuki's offer
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara bought Alistair's stew with a small worn coin and asked whether he'll go back to the counter tomorrow to report; his first contract is a rat cull in the Outer District cellars (three copper) and he would rather take it with someone. Alistair said he'll take him up on it after reporting to Mizuho.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'my first contract's a rat cull in the Outer District cellars... I'd rather take it with someone than alone.' / Alistair: 'I'll take you up on that.'

facts.subject: inn lodging
facts.fact: Alistair paid silver for a bed at the plain Guild Quarter inn and has an iron key and a wooden credit chit; the innkeeper is a woman; room is left of the stairs.
facts.evidence: The innkeeper takes the silver, slides a heavy iron key and a wooden credit chit across the counter

facts.subject: Kazuki's meeting
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara and Alistair agreed to meet at first bell at the east door for Kazuki's rat cull; Kazuki brings the torches.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'Deal! First bell, east door, I'll bring the torches.'

facts.subject: Mizuho's plain ask
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku told Alistair plainly that someone has been posting jobs past her counter (private board, no escrow, no names) and that two adventurers who took those jobs have not come back; she asked whom he met. She stamped Kazuki's rat-cull form twice.
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'Two adventurers who took those jobs haven't come back. So. Whom did you meet?'

facts.subject: report to Mizuho
facts.fact: Alistair told Mizuho the courier was dressed entirely in grey with a mask, gave no name, and said more work is available wherever grey stands at a crowd's edge.
facts.evidence: Alistair: 'He called himself a courier, dressed entirely in grey with a mask.'

facts.subject: the board's pattern
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku showed Alistair a thin older ledger with two vanished names and dates: both took private-board slips, solo, talented, no family or one waiting at home. She thinks that is how the board chooses ('people with open doors'); the courier asking if anyone expects him home puts Alistair on its list. She asked him to find who runs the board before it comes back for him, and told him and Kazuki to come to her first if anyone in grey finds either of them.
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'An open door means you're on its list. So here's what I want: find who runs that board before it comes back for you.'

facts.subject: pair contract
facts.fact: Mizuho stamped a pair contract for Alistair and Kazuki Ōhara with the guild seal: the rat cull in the cellars outside the Guild Quarter ('Rats won't kill you, but staying solo might'). She ordered breakfast for both before the queue.
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'One pair contract: you and Ōhara, the cellars outside the quarter.'

facts.subject: breakfast
facts.fact: Mizuho paid for Alistair's and Kazuki's breakfast ('She does that for new pairs. Eat it all, she counts'). Kazuki says 'it's fine' when he is not; a rookie in the hall swears by a two-copper sleep charm from the spell cart in the market; Alistair told Kazuki it is definitely a scam.
facts.evidence: SERVING GIRL: 'Mizuho paid for yours.' / Alistair: 'Definitely a scam.'

facts.subject: Yumi's cart rumor
facts.fact: Rookies in the Guild Hall talk about a spell cart in the market selling two-copper sleep charms (a wooden charm stamped with a merchant's seal).
facts.evidence: ROUND-FACED ROOKIE: 'Spell cart in the market, I'm telling you. Two coppers!'

facts.subject: rat cull terms
facts.fact: The pair contract: cellar under the cooper's row, behind a cooper's yard; the owner pays three copper per confirmed cull; rats in the grain stores. Kazuki bought four pine-pitch torches.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'Contract says cellar under the cooper's row... three copper per confirmed cull'

facts.subject: the rats
facts.fact: The rats gather in the dark corners flanking the stair, hate open flame, and bite at anything in the dark; one bit Kazuki's boot heel.
facts.evidence: the rats pouring into the black corners... 'they bite at anything in the dark'

facts.subject: awakened blade
facts.fact: In the cooper's cellar Alistair drew the Waking Relic Blade and spoke its old name; the steel woke, glowing brighter than Kazuki's torch and leaving glowing afterimages as he cut. Kazuki, awed, said swords aren't supposed to be awake.
facts.evidence: Alistair draws the Waking Relic Blade in one clean arc and speaks its old name—and the steel remembers

facts.subject: Kazuki bitten
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara was bitten on the ankles through his boots and held the bottom stair with his torch, shouting where the rats gathered.
facts.evidence: rats pouring across the grain sacks and hitting Kazuki's ankles, teeth finding flesh through boot leather

facts.subject: rat cull payout
facts.fact: Bram, the cooper whose cellar held the rats, paid Kazuki six copper for the confirmed cull, three each as posted ('Didn't think two F-ranks would manage it before noon'). Kazuki pushed four of the six toward Alistair; Alistair pocketed two copper.
facts.evidence: BRAM: 'Six copper, three each, as posted.' / Kazuki pushes four of the six coins back toward Alistair

facts.subject: Kazuki's gratitude
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara said 'Nobody ever says stuff like that to me' after Alistair told him he held the stair. He asked whether to tell Mizuho about the courier and why Alistair took the unsealed job; he said Mizuho looked scared.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'Nobody ever... says stuff like that to me.'

facts.subject: Mizuho's fear
facts.fact: Asked what she is afraid of, Mizuho Kaimaku touched her left forearm (something sits beneath her uniform sleeve) and said only: 'Another empty chair in my queue.'
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'Another empty chair in my queue.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's kitchen rule
facts.fact: Mizuho ordered Kazuki Ōhara to eat at her kitchen every dawn until he has a party ('That is not an offer, that is a schedule... guild policy'), and slid him a stamped copy of the rat-cull payout with two copper on top.
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'You eat at my kitchen every dawn until you have a party.'

facts.subject: Mizuho's warning
facts.fact: Mizuho told Alistair the board will come back to him ('exactly what it fishes for: solo, talented, no one waiting at home'); when it does he comes to her counter first, and not alone.
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'When it does, you come to this counter first. And not alone.'

facts.subject: pair amendment
facts.fact: Mizuho had Alistair and Kazuki sign a pair contract amendment so the Guild knows Kazuki answers for Alistair and Alistair answers for Kazuki. She said the forearm touch is 'an old counter habit' and told Alistair: 'Ask me again after you've come back from something. Something that costs you. Then we'll talk about what counters like this one are for.'
facts.evidence: MIZUHO: 'this is your pair contract amendment... The arm is an old counter habit.' / 'Ask me again after you've come back from something.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's dusk promise
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara said that if Alistair is not back by dusk he will tell Mizuho; Mizuho said her counter is open until the evening bell and that she counts heads.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'Fine. But if you're not back by dusk, I'm telling Mizuho.'

facts.subject: Barlow's tip
facts.fact: Barlow Kirigaya, a drunk in the Guild Quarter square, said a man in a grey coat with brass buttons slipped out toward the market not ten minutes ago, too quiet for boots that clean. Alistair saw a flicker of grey cloth and brass light at the edge of a crowd around the spell cart before it moved into the market lanes.
facts.evidence: BARLOW: 'Saw one slip out of here not ten minutes past, heading market way.'

facts.subject: Courier's wharf job
facts.fact: In a lane behind the spice stalls the grey courier said 'You came looking. That is the honest thing.' and named a night delivery at the riverside wharf after the ninth bell, alone or not at all. He left a grey-wax slip with those words; Alistair picked it up and keeps it.
facts.evidence: You came looking. That is the honest thing. ... Riverside wharf. After the ninth bell. Alone, or not at all.

facts.subject: Alistair goes alone
facts.fact: Alistair intends to go to the wharf alone (overprotective to a fault); Mizuho had said not alone and Kazuki's dusk clock is still open.
facts.evidence: Alistair will go alone

facts.subject: Alistair's purchase from Yumi
facts.fact: At the spell cart Yumi Aokiba sold Alistair a sleep charm for two coppers and a torch-glow tablet; he did not haggle. She said she can't read him at all. He briefly mentioned the grey-sealed slip; she said 'Careful with that.'
facts.evidence: Alistair buys a sleep charm for two coppers, plus a torch-glow tablet.

facts.subject: Wharf parcel
facts.fact: At the ninth bell on the riverside wharf the courier in grey gave Alistair a small brown-paper parcel tied with string: deliver to whoever waits at the pier's end, unopened, no names. A hooded man waits at the far end. Alistair took it without questions.
facts.evidence: Give this to whoever waits at the pier's end. Unopened. No names asked.

facts.subject: Kazuki told Mizuho
facts.fact: At the dusk bell Kazuki Ohara kept his word and told Mizuho Kaimaku that Alistair went after the courier toward the wharf. Mizuho closed her ledger early and said nothing aloud.
facts.evidence: Kazuki Ōhara keeps his word — he limps to Mizuho Kaimaku's counter

facts.subject: Parcel handed over
facts.fact: Alistair delivered the courier's parcel to the hooded man at the pier's end (ordinary, middle years, dockworker's build). The man checked the string knot, said 'Right on time', took the parcel, and left by a moored skiff. The courier in grey had vanished from the lamp at the pier's midpoint.
facts.evidence: Right on time. ... The courier in grey is gone.

facts.subject: Mizuho at the wharf
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku met Alistair at the pier's mouth, coat over guild clothes, and said 'Kazuki told me. I said not alone.' She asked what he carried. Alistair said he did not check the parcel and went alone so the others would not get involved. He kept the grey-wax slip.
facts.evidence: Kazuki told me. I said not alone. ... What did you carry?

facts.subject: Mizuho's morning invite
facts.fact: Mizuho Kaimaku walked Alistair off the wharf, asked nothing about the parcel or the slip (her eyes rested on his coat pocket for a second), and said the counter opens at dawn and that Kazuki eats at her kitchen every morning now; Alistair should be there too, not an order. She told him to say so before he goes next time, not after.
facts.evidence: Counter opens at dawn. Kazuki eats at my kitchen every morning now. You should be there too.

facts.subject: Day 3 morning counter
facts.fact: Day 3 dawn at the Guild Hall: Kazuki Ohara sits with a meat bun, ankle propped on a stool, and shares it with Alistair. Mizuho Kaimaku pours tea, asks nothing about the wharf, and says today's counter is two vermin culls, one grain-cart escort and the board not stamped yet; nothing for either of them until she says so.
facts.evidence: Today's counter: two vermin culls, one escort request for a grain cart, and the board's not stamped yet.

facts.subject: Rest day granted
facts.fact: Day 3 dawn: Mizuho Kaimaku allowed Alistair and Kazuki Ohara one rest day ('Rest days aren't in the rulebook. I'll allow one.') and told both to be back before the evening bell. Kazuki's ankle needs the day; Alistair accepted his invitation and helped him stand.
facts.evidence: Be back before the evening bell. Both of you.

facts.subject: Toma at the market
facts.fact: Day 3 mid-morning in the Market District, Toma Kirisawa in plain clothes at a food stall called it coincidence, bought a portion of grilled fish and rice for Alistair and a spare one, and pointed Kazuki to a bench for his ankle. He asked what two adventurers do on a day off.
facts.evidence: Well. Coincidence. Sit, sit — there's a bench right there for that ankle.

facts.subject: Toma meets Kazuki
facts.fact: At the market bench Toma Kirisawa asked Kazuki's name; Kazuki introduced himself as F-rank and Alistair as his senior in a pair contract. Toma said he cooks 'enough' and that his grandmother's kitchen taught him before the palace did, and asked what two adventurers do on a day off.
facts.evidence: Grandmother's kitchen taught me before the palace did.

facts.subject: Toma's market idea
facts.fact: Toma Kirisawa suggested a slow walk around the market with him while he shops ('A day off is mostly food and sitting'), told Kazuki his sword is long for him ('It's not fine. It's workable.') and to keep it dry, and pointed out the foxkin at the spell cart: 'I overpay her. She knows why.'
facts.evidence: Walk the market slow with me while I shop. ... I overpay her. She knows why.

facts.subject: Yumi sells Kazuki a drying charm
facts.fact: At the spell cart Yumi Aokiba greeted Toma as a regular ('Full price, same as always'), told Kazuki his secondhand long sword needed a drying charm or it would rust, flat price three copper. Toma paid for it over Kazuki's protest; Yumi said nothing is free. Kazuki said he would pay Toma back; Toma said don't bother, eat instead. Yumi told Alistair she still can't read him.
facts.evidence: Nothing here is free. He's paying. That's the whole transaction.

facts.subject: Yumi's goods and prices
facts.fact: At the cart Yumi Aokiba knotted Alistair's bootlaces as a test (he fell against the counter); she then set out a fire-starting glyph (two copper), a drying charm (three copper) and a ward against small curses (four copper, worth it in cellars), and called her heavy-paper bordered glyph card her best work: holds a full day of steady light or heat, eight silver, no discounts. She said again she can't read him and called that rude. Toma said Alistair does that to everyone.
facts.evidence: This one's my best work. Glyph card ... Eight silver. I don't discount it.

facts.subject: Alistair buys Yumi's best card
facts.fact: Alistair paid eight silver for Yumi Aokiba's best glyph card without haggling; she wrapped it herself ('Keep it dry. Wet paper warps and the script drifts'), said the bootlace knot was a test he passed 'sort of', and that his elbow was fine. Kazuki said eight silver is more than he makes in a month; Toma said flatly it was a lot for one card.
facts.evidence: That was the test. You passed. Sort of. Your elbow's fine, by the way.

facts.subject: Yumi on reading
facts.fact: Yumi Aokiba explained quietly that every customer comes with a colour (nervous grey-blue, greedy orange, in love pink) which she reads and prices off. Alistair reads as a flat line: no colour, no mood, 'like a wall where a person should be'. It has never happened before and she doesn't know why. She refused to say where the knack came from ('How I got it stays mine'). Toma and Kazuki stood by.
facts.evidence: It looks like nothing. No colour, no mood, no up or down. ... It's never happened before.

facts.subject: Yumi's goal
facts.fact: Yumi Aokiba told Alistair she wants a shop with a door, not a cart: a door that locks from the inside with her name on it. She gave no reason ('That's not part of the question').
facts.evidence: YUMI: 'A shop with a door. Not a cart. A door that locks from the inside, with my name on it.'

facts.subject: Yumi's three questions
facts.fact: Alistair bought three honest questions from Yumi with a gold coin (T38). Two used: mask or nothing (T39), her life goal (T40). One left, still his.
facts.evidence: YUMI: 'One question left. Use it or save it.'

facts.subject: Yumi's terms
facts.fact: Yumi Aokiba told Alistair it is not a yes and not a no: if it ever happens it is one job, her terms, her price. First she wants to see what fighting well means to him, his pick of test, here or somewhere private. His third bought question is still unspent.
facts.evidence: YUMI: 'Not a yes. Not a no. If this ever happens, it's one job, my terms, my price. Before any of that, I want to see what fighting well means to you.'

facts.subject: Kazuki's hope
facts.fact: Kazuki Ōhara asked aloud whether they were getting a third member, after Alistair's offer to Yumi; he stopped eating and watched the two of them.
facts.evidence: KAZUKI: 'Wait. Are we getting a third member?'
